newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2968 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2972 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a technical rebound after Wednesday's sharp falls, dealers said.
The yuan closed at 8.2972 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2955. The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2963.
The yuan opened up at an intraday high of 8.2956 but fell to consolidate around 8.2970 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2971 before rebounding slightly at the close.
Trading was active with most done at about 8.2970, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan's rebound had been expected but its upward trend was unlikely to continue with pro-yuan sentiment weakening.

"As most foreign banks allowed to conduct local currency business can now buy yuan in the interbank market, their demand (for yuan) on the foreign exchange market is no longer regarded as a strong support for the yuan," he added.
A second dealer said the yuan had fluctuated sharply in the past few days and he expected it to calm down on Friday.
He expected the yuan to remain stable between 8.2965 and 8.2970 on Friday.
The yuan closed up at 6.7382 from 6.7600 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0719 from 1.0708 against the Hong Kong dollar.
